patch.value: GH-1137: linked docs writes silently persist nonexistent workspace paths

Track GitHub issue #1137: `pm docs <id> --add` accepts and persists a local project path that does not exist, reports success, and leaves validation to a separate opt-in read. The durable dangling link then contaminates future agent context and is absent from the default health signal.

Promote path validation policy to the public SDK; return structured existing/missing/remote counts on files and docs writes; support warn and strict modes while preserving explicit forward references; include dangling linked resources in health; add CLI, SDK, MCP, history, config, and temp-workspace acceptance coverage.
pm 2026.8.28, Linux; repository-backed tracker with a nonexistent project-relative docs path
Run `pm docs <id> --add path=test/nonexistent-linked-doc.ts,note=planned coverage`; observe changed true, then run `pm docs <id> --validate-paths` to reveal the dangling path.
Linked-resource writes make path existence visible at mutation time and expose repository-configurable strict refusal plus fleet-wide health detection without prohibiting explicit forward references.
The write succeeds silently, the nonexistent path persists in the item and history, and only a separate opt-in validation call reveals it.
Agents persist false documentation provenance that is repeatedly returned as context and cannot be distinguished from a real linked resource by later readers.
